statement: New Hampshire's probate court may grant a petition to change your name, and the court cannot require you to get anyone's consent to the change.
detail: If you're incarcerated, on probation or parole, required to register as a sex offender, or convicted of certain violent felonies or crimes against a child, you must make a compelling showing that the name change is necessary, and the court must give notice to the Department of Corrections or the Department of Safety and the original prosecuting office.

source.title: New Hampshire RSA 547:3-i — Change of Name

topic: No public notice for a New Hampshire name change
statement: A New Hampshire probate court can grant a name change without public notice. The law lists changing the name of someone who resides in the county as a case needing no notice, at the discretion of the judge — so New Hampshire does not require you to publish a newspaper notice of your petition.
detail: You must reside in the county where you file your petition.

source.title: New Hampshire RSA 550:4 — Cases Requiring No Notice

topic: New Hampshire name change filing fee
statement: Filing a Name Change Petition in the Probate Division of a New Hampshire circuit court costs $170. Filing one as part of a Family Division case, such as a divorce, costs $140 instead.
detail: If you can't afford the fee, you can ask the court in writing to lower it or waive it. Certified copies of your signed order cost $10 each.

cost.note: Filing as part of a Family Division case, such as a divorce, costs $140 instead. If you can't afford the fee, you can ask the court in writing to lower it or waive it.

source.title: New Hampshire Circuit Court Filing Fees

topic: New Hampshire driver's license name change
statement: New Hampshire law requires you to notify the DMV in writing within 30 days of legally changing your name. You do this by making an appointment to bring a completed Record Change Request (DSMV 30) to a DMV office, along with your current license and legal proof of the name change, such as a certified court order, a divorce decree, or a marriage certificate.
detail: Name changes can't be done by mail. You'll get a 60-day temporary paper license at your appointment while the state mails your permanent one.

cost.note: This is for the replacement license issued as part of a name change. Other DMV transactions may carry a separate fee.

source.title: New Hampshire DMV — Update Personal Information

topic: New Hampshire driver's license gender designation
statement: To change the gender on your New Hampshire driver's license or ID, make an appointment at the DMV. Bring a completed Application for Driver License (DSMV 450), marked "Replacement" with "gender change" as the reason, your current license or ID card, and a payment of $10.00.
detail: New Hampshire's current DMV page does not list a court order or a doctor's letter as a requirement for this change.

source.title: New Hampshire DMV — Update Personal Information

topic: New Hampshire birth certificate name change
statement: New Hampshire will amend your birth record to show a new name once the clerk of the town or city where you were born receives a certified copy of a court order changing your name. The clerk enters a note that says "legal change of name per court order" and adds an "A.K.A." for your original name — it isn't erased.
detail: This process is only for people born in New Hampshire. The clerk forwards notice of the change to the state registrar.

source.title: New Hampshire RSA 5-C:87 — Initiating Amendments and Corrections to Birth Records

topic: New Hampshire birth certificate sex change
statement: New Hampshire prepares a new birth record once it receives a certified copy of a court order advising that a person born in New Hampshire has had a sex change.
detail: This is different from a name-only change: instead of adding a note to your existing record, the state prepares a new one. New Hampshire's law does not describe any path for this change that skips the court order.

source.title: New Hampshire RSA 5-C:87 — Initiating Amendments and Corrections to Birth Records

statement: Amending or correcting a New Hampshire birth record costs $10, paid by the person requesting the change. That fee is waived if the town clerk made the original error.
detail: Separately, a search for a vital record costs $15, which includes a certified copy if one is found; each additional certified copy costs $10.

cost.note: This fee is waived if the town clerk made the original error. A vital-records search costs $15 and includes one certified copy; each additional certified copy costs $10.

source.title: New Hampshire RSA 5-C:10 — Fees for Copies, Verifications and Amendments to Vital Records
